original_question: Suppose T and S are cohomologous positive closed currents with T more singular than S. Determine whether their non-pluripolar self-products satisfy <T^n> <= <S^n>.
target_in_paper: Section 2.1, Question 10 (Boucksom-Eyssidieux-Guedj-Zeriahi): the monotonicity problem for top non-pluripolar self-products of cohomologous currents ordered by singularities.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core of the paper's exact open problem: it uses the right objects (cohomologous positive closed currents), the right singularity ordering (T more singular than S), and the right desired conclusion (the measure inequality ⟨T^n⟩ <= ⟨S^n⟩ for non-pluripolar top self-products). This is essentially Question 10 in the paper.
missing_details: The ambient setting should be stated: X is a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension n.
T and S should be specified as positive closed (1,1)-currents, not arbitrary currents.
The notation T ∼ S should be unpacked as 'T and S lie in the same real (1,1)-cohomology class'.

The phrase 'T more singular than S' should be made stand-alone by expressing it in terms of potentials: after choosing a common smooth representative θ of the class, write T = θ + dd^c u and S = θ + dd^c v with u <= v + O(1).
The symbol ⟨T^n⟩ should be defined as the non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère product via bounded truncations, as in Definition 2.1.
The inequality should be specified as an inequality of positive Radon measures, not merely of total masses.

To reflect the paper's intent precisely, the question should note that this is asked in full generality, i.e. without the extra 'small unbounded locus' assumption under which the inequality is already known.
The scope should remain the top self-product only; the paper does not ask here about mixed non-pluripolar products or broader variants.
refined_question: Let X be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension n, and let T and S be cohomologous positive closed (1,1)-currents on X. Choose a smooth closed real (1,1)-form θ in their common cohomology class and write T = θ + dd^c u and S = θ + dd^c v with u and v θ-plurisubharmonic. Assume u <= v + C on X, i.e. T is more singular than S. If ⟨T^n⟩ and ⟨S^n⟩ denote the non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère products defined by bounded truncation, for example ⟨T^n⟩ = lim_{j→∞} 1_{u>-j}(θ + dd^c max(u,-j))^n, must one always have ⟨T^n⟩ <= ⟨S^n⟩ as positive measures, without assuming that T and S have small unbounded locus?
justification: The draft is targeting Question 10 in Section 2.1. The paper first defines the non-pluripolar product in Definition 2.1, then recalls that [BEGZ10, Theorem 1.16] proves the inequality ⟨T^n⟩ <= ⟨S^n⟩ for cohomologous positive closed currents when T is more singular than S and both currents have small unbounded locus, and immediately asks whether the same inequality remains true in full generality. The refined version stays exactly on that question, adding only the ambient compact Kähler setting, the bidegree of the currents, the measure-theoretic meaning of the inequality, and a stand-alone unpacking of the singularity order and of the non-pluripolar product notation.
